name: Alaska
keyNotes: Alaska uses boroughs not counties — 19 organized boroughs plus unorganized areas
Low inventory state — remote and rural parcels dominate
Bidding method varies by municipality — always contact borough directly before registering
summary: Alaska operates through boroughs (not counties). The Matanuska-Susitna and Fairbanks North Star boroughs occasionally sell tax-foreclosed properties. Statute: AS §29.45.
typeWhy: Alaska sells the property outright through borough-level tax foreclosure auctions — the buyer receives a deed, not a lien. Some boroughs allow a 1-year redemption period. AS §29.45.
rateWhy: Alaska has no fixed statutory interest rate on tax sales. Bidding is market-driven, with prices determined by competitive auction at the borough level. AS §29.45.
notBeginnerReason: Borough-based system, limited inventory, federal land ownership restricts most parcels. Requires local connections.
beginnerTip: Not a recommended starting state. If pursuing Alaska, focus on Matanuska-Susitna Borough which has the most consistent auction activity.
risks: Federal land ownership restricts a large percentage of available parcels
Remote properties have extreme logistics costs
Very low inventory — not a reliable primary market
ddExtra: Verify parcel is not federal, state, or Native corporation land before bidding
Check BLM land atlas for ownership classification
Confirm road access — many parcels are landlocked or fly-in only

steps: Identify your target borough at commerce.alaska.gov
Contact the borough assessor or tax collector directly — no centralized state system
Request the tax foreclosure list when available
Register and attend the auction per borough instructions — most require in-person attendance

rules.statute: AS §29.45.290–§29.45.500 (Municipal Taxation — Enforcement of Tax Liens)
rules.structure: Alaska has boroughs (not counties) + home rule municipalities. Only taxing municipalities (25 total) levy property tax. Rural Alaska unorganized areas generally have no property tax.
rules.critical: ⚡ Alaska does NOT hold public tax auctions where anyone can bid on tax-delinquent property. Municipality files court petition, acquires property through judicial decree, then sells through its own process.

process.step1: Delinquent taxes become lien on property.
process.step2: Municipality files petition with Superior Court for judicial foreclosure (AS §29.45.320, §29.45.330).
process.step3: Publication: delinquent tax list published in newspaper for 4 weeks (or posted if no newspaper).
process.step4: Within 10 days of first publication: municipality mails certified mail notice to owner.
process.step5: 30-day answer period: interested parties may file answer with court (AS §29.45.370).
process.step6: Court enters Judgment and Decree of Foreclosure. Property transfers to municipality.
process.step8: Municipality sells foreclosed property (sealed bids, public auction, or other process per municipal ordinance).

auction.frequency: As scheduled by each municipality. FNSB: at least every 2 years.

platform.anchorage: Sealed bid auction (typical). Properties listed at muni.org/Departments/hlb/pages/resforeclosedproperties.aspx. 2026 properties listed.
platform.other: Each municipality sets its own process per AS §29.45.460(b)

confirmed2026.fnsb: August 28, 2026 — Fairbanks North Star Borough — CONFIRMED OFFICIAL (fnsb.gov)
confirmed2026.anchorage: 2026 properties listed at muni.org — sale date TBD. Typical: sealed bid process.
confirmed2026.fnsb_interest: FNSB delinquency: 5% penalty + 8%/yr simple interest on taxes due

otc.name: N/A — Alaska municipal foreclosure only. No OTC lien cert sales.
otc.note: Contact individual municipalities for surplus/unsold foreclosed property listings.

subTax.name: N/A — No private lien cert holders in Alaska

delinquencyInterest.statute: AS §29.45 — rates set by each municipality

redemption.period: 1 year from date property transferred to municipality by court decree
redemption.amounts: Lien amount + penalties + interest + costs (including AS §29.45.440(a) costs)
redemption.possession: Owner may reside in property during redemption period. Municipality may declare immediate forfeiture if owner damages property.
redemption.preDecree: Owner may stop foreclosure anytime before court transfers property by paying full delinquency.

repurchaseRight.period: 10 years from date foreclosure completed (if property not yet sold to new owner)
repurchaseRight.amounts: Debt amount + interest ≤15%/yr from foreclosure judgment date + delinquent taxes that would have accrued + maintenance/management costs exceeding rental income + insurance + HOA dues
repurchaseRight.note: 10-year right expires if municipality sells property to third party

deedPath.name: Municipality acquires by court decree → sells to buyer
deedPath.titleEffect: Buyer gets title to property. Mortgage and other liens eliminated.
deedPath.anchorageProcess: MOA: sealed bids generally. Property profiles (litigation guarantee + vicinity map) available before sale.

surplus.name: Excess Sale Proceeds
surplus.process: Upon sale: municipality provides written notice to former owner of excess amount and claim procedure. Claim must be filed within 6 months — permanently barred after.
surplus.scope: Applies if property held <10 years after redemption period and NOT designated for public purpose
surplus.anchorageNote: ⚡ Anchorage MOA: 'A claim for the excess filed after six months of the date of sale is forever barred.' Municipality sends written notice of excess and claim procedure.
surplus.noticeRequired: Municipality MUST give written notice of surplus and claim procedure to former owner (AS §29.45.460(c))

es.summary: Alaska opera a través de boroughs. Los boroughs de Matanuska-Susitna y Fairbanks North Star ocasionalmente venden propiedades embargadas. Estatuto: AS §29.45.
es.typeWhy: Alaska es un estado de escritura porque los boroughs venden directamente la propiedad embargada por impuestos, transfiriendo el título al comprador en la subasta (AS §29.45).
es.rateWhy: La tasa varía por borough ya que no existe una tasa estatutaria fija. Cada borough establece sus propios términos de venta según su regulación local.
es.notBeginnerReason: Sistema basado en boroughs, inventario limitado, la propiedad federal restringe la mayoría de las parcelas.
es.beginnerTip: No es un estado inicial recomendado. Si busca Alaska, enfóquese en Matanuska-Susitna que tiene la actividad más consistente.
risks: La propiedad federal restringe gran porcentaje de parcelas
Propiedades remotas con costos de logística extremos
Las reglas del borough varían significativamente
ddExtra: Verifique que la parcela no sea tierra federal, estatal o de corporación nativa
Revise el atlas de BLM para clasificación de propiedad
Confirme acceso vial — muchas parcelas solo accesibles por avión

steps: Identifique su borough objetivo en commerce.alaska.gov
Contacte al tasador o recaudador del borough directamente — sin sistema estatal centralizado
Solicite la lista de ejecuciones fiscales cuando esté disponible
Regístrese y asista según las instrucciones del borough
